raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Summary

Fixes #56419. On the CPU GDN speculative path, `num_accepted == 0` makes the native convolution kernel violate its `[1, seqlen]` precondition. The Python fallback also reads history at offset `-1` and rolls rejected draft tokens into the convolution state.

The native path additionally cannot represent a valid shrunken step whose previous step accepted more tokens than the current step carries. Those rows need the Python fallback rather than a kernel call with invalid arguments.

## Changes

- Route batches with zero acceptance or acceptance outside the native kernel contract through the Python fallback.
- Clamp zero acceptance to history offset 0, compute draft outputs over the intact history, and skip the convolution-state roll for that row.
- Preserve the previous-step acceptance semantics for shrunken steps. Do not clamp the history offset to the current query length.
- If acceptance exceeds the actual stored history, use the latest valid history window and emit a one-time warning.
- Add regressions for zero-acceptance state preservation, native-kernel avoidance, and acceptance beyond the stored history. The existing cross-step regression also covers the valid `accepted > current q_i` case.

## Testing

Rebuilt on current main `e4a5b55373` and ran on an arm64 Mac with `VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu`:

- The three new regressions fail against the unfixed implementation and pass with this change.
- `pytest tests/kernels/mamba/cpu/test_cpu_gdn_ops.py -k "spec_forward or causal_conv1d_torch" --deselect "tests/kernels/mamba/cpu/test_cpu_gdn_ops.py::test_spec_forward_conv_tracks_accepted_tokens[True]"`: **11 passed, 144 deselected**. This includes the existing fallback regression for uneven current query lengths and previous-step acceptance counts.
- Ruff format, Ruff check, and `git diff --check` pass on both changed files.
- The deselected native parameter case stops during test setup because this environment's `_C` binary has no `causal_conv1d_weight_pack`. A whole-file run is likewise not green here because that binary lacks the current CPU GDN symbols. These are not reported as passing tests, and native AMX execution remains a CI/hardware validation item.

## AI assistance disclosure

This change was prepared with AI assistance (Kimi). The diff and the verification results above were checked during preparation.

nodes.body:
Hi @he-yufeng,

Thanks for picking this up so fast. I tested this branch and it doesn't close the
crash on my setup — reporting it here rather than letting you find it after merge.

**Method:** `gdn_attention.py` from this branch (`2ad309c5`) copied over the
installed file in the `vllm-openai-cpu:v0.29.0` image, MTP K=4,
`--enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder`. I confirmed the patch
was actually live by line number rather than assuming it — unpatched the crash is
at `:427`, patched it moves to `:433`, exactly the +6 lines this PR inserts. A
plain completion returned 200 first, so the engine was healthy up to the trigger.

| with this branch | result |
|---|---|
| plain completion (control) | 200, alive |
| strict tools + `tool_choice:"auto"` | **500, dead** — same `num_accepted_tokenw at `:433` |
| `response_format: json_schema`, ordinary nested schema | **500, dead** — `_spec_aware_nonspec:576`, `tensormust be contiguous at last dimension` |

On the second row: that's a **second, distinct defect** that this PR correctly
doesn't touch (no reference to `_spec_aware_nonspec` or
`fused_sigmoid_gating_delta_rule_update_cpu` in the diff). It reaches the *non*-
speculative fallback with `scheduled_spec_decode_tokens={}`, so speculation is
suppressed for that step rather than rejected. I've rewritten #56419 to document
both paths properly — including withdrawing a retraction in that issue that had
wrongly dismissed this contiguity failure as a mis-recorded traceback. It's real
my earlier edit was the error. Apologies for having sent you at a half-picture.

On the first row, offered tentatively: the new guard checks
`num_accepted[:num_spec_decodes] > 0`, and the native call hands the **same
slice** to the kernel. For control to reach the kernel at all, every element must
already have been `> 0` — which leaves the other half of `[1, seqlen]`, i.e.
`num_accepted > seqlen`. I lost the test machine before capturing the failing
step's actual values, so that's inference, not measurement.

**Caveat on my test:** I backported this branch's Python file onto v0.29.0 rather
than building `main`; `_custom_ops.py` and the C++ kernel stayed at v0.29.0. If
`main` also changed the kernel or that shim, my result wouldn't reflect it —
worth discounting accordingly.

I also tried three local fixes for the contiguity path (forcing `q`/`k`/`v`
contiguous at that call site, the same at the sibling call site, and normalizing
`mixed_qkv`/`a`/`b` at the `cpu_gdn_attention_core` entry point). All three still
crashed with the traceback moving in step with my inserted lines, so it isn't a
one-line `.contiguous()` and I haven't isolated which argument is at fault.

Happy to run any diagnostic patch you want against the real trigger — I have a
reproduction and can turn it around quickly.

@ixcans Your retest was right, and your inference held up in the code. The zero-check was only half the contract.

**What the kernel actually validates** (`csrc/cpu/sgl-kernels/conv.cpp`, the `causal_conv1d_update_cpu` TORCH_CHECKs): per sequence, `num_accepted >= 1`, `num_accepted <= seqlen` (the `q_i` from `seq_lens[0]` that the guard view-shapes `x` with), and `num_accepted - 1 + width - 1 <= state_len`. My first patch only covered the first one, so a shrunken step (`num_accepted > q_i`) sailed through my guard and died at `:433` exactly as you measured.

**What changed in `dab4070a76`:**

- The native-path guard now mirrors all three checks; any sequence outside the contract routes the whole batch through the fallback loop.
- The fallback clamps instead of fabricating: `acc_eff = min(max(acc, 0), q_i)` for the history offset and the roll, `q_eff = min(q_i, state_len)` for the roll width, so only tokens the step actually produced are committed, and a `warning_once` logs the shrink with the real `num_accepted` and `q_i` values.
- New regression test `test_spec_forward_over_reported_acceptance_is_clamped`: over-reported acceptance never reaches the native kernel (asserted by making the native call fail on contact), the buffer tail is exactly the produced sequence, and the draft outputs match a direct reference convolution at the clamped offset.

**Verification on my side (Mac, `VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu`):** full `tests/kernels/mamba/cpu/test_cpu_gdn_ops.py` is 93 passed / 41 skipped / 0 failed. That count includes a rebuilt `vllm._C` — my earlier run of this file had 81 failures that were purely the stale `.so` in my venv (missing `fused_gdn_gating_cpu`/`chunk_gated_delta_rule_cpu`), so I rebuilt it this round to make the run meaningful.

**The ask:** could you rerun the strict-tools trigger on this head? If the clamp path fires, the `warning_once` line will print the actual `num_accepted` vs `q_i`, which finally names the case instead of our joint inference. If it still crashes I'd want that line plus the traceback, and I'll keep digging.

**On the `json_schema` row:** agreed it's a separate defect in the non-speculative fallback (`_spec_aware_nonspec:576`, contiguity at last dim) and correctly out of scope here. I read your updated #56419 writeup; once this row is closed I'll take a swing at that path as its own PR rather than bundling it into this one. Your three `.contiguous()` attempts moving the traceback in step with the inserted lines suggests the non-contiguous tensor is produced upstream of the call site, so I'll start from where the fallback's `mixed_qkv` is sliced rather than at the call.

Fixed the branch hygiene: pre-commit and DCO are both green at 9ff2c4e (the E501 wrap, a typo-hook false positive on `TORCH_CHECKs`, and the format drift from the rebase). No behavior change from 6ef142b.

@ixcans whenever you have a slot, this head is the one to retest.

@he-yufeng Retested on `9ff2c4e4`. **The clamp fires and it holds — Path A is fixed.**

I diffed `9ff2c4e4` against `6ef142b` before rerunning: the only deltas are the comment
reword and two line-wraps, so your "no behavior change" is confirmed independently rather
than assumed. Ran the full matrix on the new head anyway.

## The `warning_once` you asked for

Five firings, five distinct pairs, no crash:

```
GDN CPU spec path: num_accepted=3 exceeds the step's query length 2; committing only the produced tokens
GDN CPU spec path: num_accepted=4 exceeds the step's query length 2; committing only the produced tokens
GDN CPU spec path: num_accepted=4 exceeds the step's query length 3; committing only the produced tokens
GDN CPU spec path: num_accepted=5 exceeds the step's query length 2; committing only the produced tokens
GDN CPU spec path: num_accepted=5 exceeds the step's query length 3; committing only the produced tokens
```

So it is the **upper** bound, our joint inference was right, and the overshoot is **not a
fixed arity** — it varies with both `num_accepted` and `q_i`. That argues for the clamp over
any fixed-offset assumption.

## Results on `9ff2c4e4`

| case | result |
|---|---|
| plain completion (control) | 200, alive |
| strict tools + `tool_choice:"auto"` | 200, alive |
| nested `json_schema`, x12 at `max_tokens: 700` | **12/12, 0 errors, 0 restarts** |

Speculative decoding stayed fully active throughout (545 accepted / 558 drafted, mean
acceptance length 4.76, 97.7% draft acceptance), so this is not "it passed because
speculation quietly stopped."

**Controlled A/B.** Same rig, same engine, same payloads, same load profile; the only
variable is your patch:

| build | nested `json_schema` x12 |
|---|---|
| stock, + my index repack only | **3/12 — engine dead at request 4** (`num_accepted_tokens must be in [1, seqlen]`) |
| **your head, + the same repack** | **12/12 clean** |

## Two corrections to my previous report

**1. My earlier "does not fix it" was measured on a dirtier backport than I implied.**
Diffing your head against the release file I patch gives 7 hunks, but only 5 are yours — the
other two delete `cpu_gdn_attention_core_fake` and the `fake_impl=` argument to
`direct_register_custom_op`, which is unrelated `main` drift that changes torch.compile fake
registration. Last time I copied the whole head file, so that rode along. This time I applied
**only your 5 hunks** and kept the release's `fake_impl`, so the result measures one variable.

**2. "Rerun the strict-tools trigger" does not do what we both assumed.** My first run on
your previous head with strict tools died — but at `_spec_aware_nonspec`, the contiguity
defect, not your code. I nearly reported that as "still broken." A stock control on the
identical payload died at the **same line**, so the crash site was unchanged and that payload
never reaches `_spec_forward` at all on either build.

The consequence is worth stating plainly: **which path a request lands in is
payload-shape-dependent, not trigger-class-dependent.** The "strict tools ⇒ Path A,
`json_schema` ⇒ Path B" split I gave you earlier is wrong; either trigger can reach either
path. To exercise your fix I had to clear the contiguity defect *first*, then drive sustained
load — a single nested-schema request passed with `num_accepted` always `[1]`, and it took 12
sequential requests before the violation appeared at all. A single green request proves
nothing here.

## On the contiguity path — you don't need to go hunting

You said you'd start from where the fallback's `mixed_qkv` is sliced. I isolated it after my
last comment, and it isn't there. The offending argument to
`fused_sigmoid_gating_delta_rule_update_cpu` is **`initial_state_indices`**:

```
initial_state_indices: shape=(1,) stride=(5,) dtype=torch.int32
                       is_contiguous()=True   stride(-1)=5
```

The kernel's precondition is `stride(-1) == 1`, not full contiguity — on healthy calls it
accepts `initial_state_source` with `is_contiguous()=False` because *that* tensor's last-dim
stride is 1. Every data tensor (`q`/`k`/`v`/`a`/`b`/`mixed_qkv`) had last-dim stride 1 on the
crashing call, which is why my three earlier `.contiguous()` patches all missed.

Origin, in `v1/attention/backends/gdn_attn.py`, the `spec_sequence_masks is None` branch:

```python
non_spec_state_indices_tensor = block_table_tensor[:, 0]
```

`block_table_tensor` is `(N, num_spec + 1)`, so this basic-indexing **view** carries stride
`(num_spec + 1,)` — 5 at K=4. The sibling `block_table_tensor[mask, : num_spec + 1]` is
*advanced* indexing and therefore a copy, which is why the speculative path never trips.

**And the existing guard cannot work.** `mamba/ops/cpu/gdn_attention.py` already has
`state_indices_tensor = state_indices_tensor.contiguous()` for exactly this, but when the
batch holds a single non-spec decode the tensor has one element, and PyTorch reports
`is_contiguous() == True` for any tensor with `numel <= 1` regardless of stride — so it
returns `self` and the stride-5 view reaches the kernel untouched. The bug hides behind a
line that looks like the fix.

Confirmed by forcing a genuine packed copy (`torch.empty(...).copy_(...)`, **not**
`.contiguous()`) on the read-only index arguments: the contiguity error disappears. That
repack is what let me reach your code path at all. Suggested fix is to pack it at the
producer in `gdn_attn.py`, or check `stride(-1) == 1` explicitly at the call site;
`.contiguous()` is not sufficient anywhere a length-1 batch is possible.

## One correctness question on the clamp

The clamp stops the crash, and I want to be clear I verified that and not more. It also
silently changes which history window is read for a shrunken step. Across 14 requests I saw
no garbage output, but that does not establish the conv state stays numerically correct under
sustained clamping — my runs can't distinguish "correct" from "plausible". Since the
underlying inconsistency looks like it originates in `build()` — `spec_query_start_loc` is
this step's scheduled tokens while `num_accepted_tokens` is the previous step's sampler
result, with nothing tying them together — it may be worth deciding whether the conv path
should tolerate the pair or the metadata should never emit it. Not a blocker on this PR from
where I sit; it fixes a real crash and I'd take it.

Caveat on my setup, unchanged: I backport your Python file onto a released CPU image rather
than building `main`, so `_custom_ops.py` and the C++ kernel stay at that release. If `main`
also moved those, discount accordingly.

Happy to run anything else against this reproduction.

@ixcans Thanks for the A/B — 3/12 dead vs 12/12 clean on the same rig is the proof this needed, and the varying overshoot (num_accepted up to 5 against q_i of 2-3) settles why a fixed offset was never the right shape. The warning firing exactly on the over-contract cases and nowhere else is the behavior the field report wanted.

With your corner covered and CI green, this is ready for maintainer review on my side.

This pull request has merge conflicts that must be resolved before it can be
merged. Please rebase the PR, @he-yufeng.

https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/working-with-forks/syncing-a-fork

Rebuilt this on current main (`e4a5b55373`) and pushed `2697107688`. The conflict is resolved and GitHub now reports the PR as mergeable.

The rebuild also caught a semantic problem in my earlier clamp. `num_accepted` describes the previous step, while `q_i` is the current step's query length. Current main's `test_spec_forward_conv_tracks_accepted_tokens` explicitly exercises a valid row where the previous acceptance count is larger than the current query length, and that test failed with `min(acc, q_i)`. The fallback now clamps only to the actual stored history, not to current `q_i`. Zero acceptance still uses offset 0 and skips the state roll; acceptance beyond the stored history uses the latest valid window.

Local verification on this head is 11 passed for the related Python spec/conv tests, including that existing cross-step regression and the three new cases. Ruff and diff checks pass. The native parameter case cannot run in this checkout because its `_C` binary lacks `causal_conv1d_weight_pack`, so I am not claiming a whole-file or native-hardware pass.

@ixcans your earlier A/B established the crash fix on the previous head. If your rig is available, a retest of this rebuilt head would be useful because it preserves the valid shrunken-step history instead of clamping it to current `q_i`.

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

@@ -846,6 +846,216 @@ def test_spec_forward_conv_tracks_accepted_tokens(
             )
 
 
+@torch.inference_mode()
+def test_spec_forward_zero_acceptance_preserves_conv_state(
+    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch,
+) -> None:
+    """A fully rejected step computes over history without moving the buffer."""
+    dim = 96
+    num_spec = 4
+    state_len = num_spec + CONV_KERNEL - 2
+    torch.manual_seed(0)
+
+    stored = torch.randn(1, dim, state_len)
+    x_seq = torch.randn(num_spec, dim)
+    weight = torch.randn(dim, 1, CONV_KERNEL)
+    bias = torch.randn(dim)
+    captured = {}
+
+    def grab_rearrange(conv_out):
+        captured["conv_out"] = conv_out.clone()
+        return tuple(conv_out.unsqueeze(0).chunk(3, dim=-1)[i] for i in range(3))
+
+    layer = types.SimpleNamespace(
+        activation="silu",
+        conv1d=types.SimpleNamespace(weight=weight, bias=bias),
+        A_log=None,
+        dt_bias=None,
+        rearrange_mixed_qkv=grab_rearrange,
+    )
+    metadata = GDNAttentionMetadata(
+        num_prefills=0,
+        num_prefill_tokens=0,
+        num_decodes=0,
+        num_decode_tokens=0,
+        num_spec_decodes=1,
+        num_spec_decode_tokens=num_spec,
+        num_actual_tokens=num_spec,
+        spec_state_indices_tensor=torch.zeros(1, num_spec, dtype=torch.int32),
+        spec_query_start_loc=torch.tensor([0, num_spec], dtype=torch.int32),
+        num_accepted_tokens=torch.tensor([0], dtype=torch.int32),
+    )
+
+    conv_buf = stored.clone()
+    monkeypatch.setattr(
+        gdn_attention.ops,
+        "fused_sigmoid_gating_delta_rule_update_spec_cpu",
+        lambda **kwargs: kwargs["q"],
+    )
+    monkeypatch.setattr(torch.cpu, "_is_amx_tile_supported", lambda: False)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(gdn_attention, "is_arm_bf16", lambda: False)
+    gdn_attention._spec_forward(
+        layer=layer,
+        attn_metadata_i=metadata,
+        mixed_qkv_spec=x_seq.clone(),
+        b_spec=torch.randn(num_spec, dim),
+        a_spec=torch.randn(num_spec, dim),
+        conv_buf=conv_buf,
+        ssm_state=torch.zeros(1, 2, 2, 2),
+        width=CONV_KERNEL,
+        state_len=state_len,
+    )
+
+    torch.testing.assert_close(conv_buf, stored, atol=0, rtol=0)
+    ref_in = torch.cat(
+        [stored[0, :, : CONV_KERNEL - 1], x_seq.transpose(0, 1)], dim=-1
+    ).unsqueeze(0)
+    ref = F.silu(F.conv1d(ref_in, weight, bias, groups=dim))[0].transpose(0, 1)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(captured["conv_out"], ref, atol=1e-4, rtol=1e-4)
+
+
+def test_spec_forward_zero_acceptance_never_reaches_native_conv(
+    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch,
+) -> None:
+    """A batch with a fully rejected sequence avoids the native conv kernel."""
+    dim = 96
+    num_spec = 4
+    state_len = num_spec + CONV_KERNEL - 2

+

+        lambda **kwargs: kwargs["q"],
+    )
+
+    layer = types.SimpleNamespace(
+        activation="silu",
+        conv1d=types.SimpleNamespace(

+        A_log=None,
+        dt_bias=None,
+        rearrange_mixed_qkv=lambda x: tuple(

Hi @he-yufeng,

Thanks for picking this up so fast. I tested this branch and it doesn't close the
crash on my setup — reporting it here rather than letting you find it after merge.

**Method:** `gdn_attention.py` from this branch (`2ad309c5`) copied over the
installed file in the `vllm-openai-cpu:v0.29.0` image, MTP K=4,
`--enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder`. I confirmed the patch
was actually live by line number rather than assuming it — unpatched the crash is
at `:427`, patched it moves to `:433`, exactly the +6 lines this PR inserts. A
plain completion returned 200 first, so the engine was healthy up to the trigger.

| with this branch | result |
|---|---|
| plain completion (control) | 200, alive |
| strict tools + `tool_choice:"auto"` | **500, dead** — same `num_accepted_tokenw at `:433` |
| `response_format: json_schema`, ordinary nested schema | **500, dead** — `_spec_aware_nonspec:576`, `tensormust be contiguous at last dimension` |

On the second row: that's a **second, distinct defect** that this PR correctly
doesn't touch (no reference to `_spec_aware_nonspec` or
`fused_sigmoid_gating_delta_rule_update_cpu` in the diff). It reaches the *non*-
speculative fallback with `scheduled_spec_decode_tokens={}`, so speculation is
suppressed for that step rather than rejected. I've rewritten #56419 to document
both paths properly — including withdrawing a retraction in that issue that had
wrongly dismissed this contiguity failure as a mis-recorded traceback. It's real
my earlier edit was the error. Apologies for having sent you at a half-picture.

On the first row, offered tentatively: the new guard checks
`num_accepted[:num_spec_decodes] > 0`, and the native call hands the **same
slice** to the kernel. For control to reach the kernel at all, every element must
already have been `> 0` — which leaves the other half of `[1, seqlen]`, i.e.
`num_accepted > seqlen`. I lost the test machine before capturing the failing
step's actual values, so that's inference, not measurement.

**Caveat on my test:** I backported this branch's Python file onto v0.29.0 rather
than building `main`; `_custom_ops.py` and the C++ kernel stayed at v0.29.0. If
`main` also changed the kernel or that shim, my result wouldn't reflect it —
worth discounting accordingly.

I also tried three local fixes for the contiguity path (forcing `q`/`k`/`v`
contiguous at that call site, the same at the sibling call site, and normalizing
`mixed_qkv`/`a`/`b` at the `cpu_gdn_attention_core` entry point). All three still
crashed with the traceback moving in step with my inserted lines, so it isn't a
one-line `.contiguous()` and I haven't isolated which argument is at fault.

Happy to run any diagnostic patch you want against the real trigger — I have a
reproduction and can turn it around quickly.

@ixcans Your retest was right, and your inference held up in the code. The zero-check was only half the contract.

**What the kernel actually validates** (`csrc/cpu/sgl-kernels/conv.cpp`, the `causal_conv1d_update_cpu` TORCH_CHECKs): per sequence, `num_accepted >= 1`, `num_accepted <= seqlen` (the `q_i` from `seq_lens[0]` that the guard view-shapes `x` with), and `num_accepted - 1 + width - 1 <= state_len`. My first patch only covered the first one, so a shrunken step (`num_accepted > q_i`) sailed through my guard and died at `:433` exactly as you measured.

**What changed in `dab4070a76`:**

- The native-path guard now mirrors all three checks; any sequence outside the contract routes the whole batch through the fallback loop.
- The fallback clamps instead of fabricating: `acc_eff = min(max(acc, 0), q_i)` for the history offset and the roll, `q_eff = min(q_i, state_len)` for the roll width, so only tokens the step actually produced are committed, and a `warning_once` logs the shrink with the real `num_accepted` and `q_i` values.
- New regression test `test_spec_forward_over_reported_acceptance_is_clamped`: over-reported acceptance never reaches the native kernel (asserted by making the native call fail on contact), the buffer tail is exactly the produced sequence, and the draft outputs match a direct reference convolution at the clamped offset.

**Verification on my side (Mac, `VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu`):** full `tests/kernels/mamba/cpu/test_cpu_gdn_ops.py` is 93 passed / 41 skipped / 0 failed. That count includes a rebuilt `vllm._C` — my earlier run of this file had 81 failures that were purely the stale `.so` in my venv (missing `fused_gdn_gating_cpu`/`chunk_gated_delta_rule_cpu`), so I rebuilt it this round to make the run meaningful.

**The ask:** could you rerun the strict-tools trigger on this head? If the clamp path fires, the `warning_once` line will print the actual `num_accepted` vs `q_i`, which finally names the case instead of our joint inference. If it still crashes I'd want that line plus the traceback, and I'll keep digging.

**On the `json_schema` row:** agreed it's a separate defect in the non-speculative fallback (`_spec_aware_nonspec:576`, contiguity at last dim) and correctly out of scope here. I read your updated #56419 writeup; once this row is closed I'll take a swing at that path as its own PR rather than bundling it into this one. Your three `.contiguous()` attempts moving the traceback in step with the inserted lines suggests the non-contiguous tensor is produced upstream of the call site, so I'll start from where the fallback's `mixed_qkv` is sliced rather than at the call.

Fixed the branch hygiene: pre-commit and DCO are both green at 9ff2c4e (the E501 wrap, a typo-hook false positive on `TORCH_CHECKs`, and the format drift from the rebase). No behavior change from 6ef142b.

@ixcans whenever you have a slot, this head is the one to retest.

@he-yufeng Retested on `9ff2c4e4`. **The clamp fires and it holds — Path A is fixed.**

I diffed `9ff2c4e4` against `6ef142b` before rerunning: the only deltas are the comment
reword and two line-wraps, so your "no behavior change" is confirmed independently rather
than assumed. Ran the full matrix on the new head anyway.

## The `warning_once` you asked for

Five firings, five distinct pairs, no crash:

```
GDN CPU spec path: num_accepted=3 exceeds the step's query length 2; committing only the produced tokens
GDN CPU spec path: num_accepted=4 exceeds the step's query length 2; committing only the produced tokens
GDN CPU spec path: num_accepted=4 exceeds the step's query length 3; committing only the produced tokens
GDN CPU spec path: num_accepted=5 exceeds the step's query length 2; committing only the produced tokens
GDN CPU spec path: num_accepted=5 exceeds the step's query length 3; committing only the produced tokens
```

So it is the **upper** bound, our joint inference was right, and the overshoot is **not a
fixed arity** — it varies with both `num_accepted` and `q_i`. That argues for the clamp over
any fixed-offset assumption.

## Results on `9ff2c4e4`

| case | result |
|---|---|
| plain completion (control) | 200, alive |
| strict tools + `tool_choice:"auto"` | 200, alive |
| nested `json_schema`, x12 at `max_tokens: 700` | **12/12, 0 errors, 0 restarts** |

Speculative decoding stayed fully active throughout (545 accepted / 558 drafted, mean
acceptance length 4.76, 97.7% draft acceptance), so this is not "it passed because
speculation quietly stopped."

**Controlled A/B.** Same rig, same engine, same payloads, same load profile; the only
variable is your patch:

| build | nested `json_schema` x12 |
|---|---|
| stock, + my index repack only | **3/12 — engine dead at request 4** (`num_accepted_tokens must be in [1, seqlen]`) |
| **your head, + the same repack** | **12/12 clean** |

## Two corrections to my previous report

**1. My earlier "does not fix it" was measured on a dirtier backport than I implied.**
Diffing your head against the release file I patch gives 7 hunks, but only 5 are yours — the
other two delete `cpu_gdn_attention_core_fake` and the `fake_impl=` argument to
`direct_register_custom_op`, which is unrelated `main` drift that changes torch.compile fake
registration. Last time I copied the whole head file, so that rode along. This time I applied
**only your 5 hunks** and kept the release's `fake_impl`, so the result measures one variable.

**2. "Rerun the strict-tools trigger" does not do what we both assumed.** My first run on
your previous head with strict tools died — but at `_spec_aware_nonspec`, the contiguity
defect, not your code. I nearly reported that as "still broken." A stock control on the
identical payload died at the **same line**, so the crash site was unchanged and that payload
never reaches `_spec_forward` at all on either build.

The consequence is worth stating plainly: **which path a request lands in is
payload-shape-dependent, not trigger-class-dependent.** The "strict tools ⇒ Path A,
`json_schema` ⇒ Path B" split I gave you earlier is wrong; either trigger can reach either
path. To exercise your fix I had to clear the contiguity defect *first*, then drive sustained
load — a single nested-schema request passed with `num_accepted` always `[1]`, and it took 12
sequential requests before the violation appeared at all. A single green request proves
nothing here.

## On the contiguity path — you don't need to go hunting

You said you'd start from where the fallback's `mixed_qkv` is sliced. I isolated it after my
last comment, and it isn't there. The offending argument to
`fused_sigmoid_gating_delta_rule_update_cpu` is **`initial_state_indices`**:

```
initial_state_indices: shape=(1,) stride=(5,) dtype=torch.int32
                       is_contiguous()=True   stride(-1)=5
```

The kernel's precondition is `stride(-1) == 1`, not full contiguity — on healthy calls it
accepts `initial_state_source` with `is_contiguous()=False` because *that* tensor's last-dim
stride is 1. Every data tensor (`q`/`k`/`v`/`a`/`b`/`mixed_qkv`) had last-dim stride 1 on the
crashing call, which is why my three earlier `.contiguous()` patches all missed.

Origin, in `v1/attention/backends/gdn_attn.py`, the `spec_sequence_masks is None` branch:

```python
non_spec_state_indices_tensor = block_table_tensor[:, 0]
```

`block_table_tensor` is `(N, num_spec + 1)`, so this basic-indexing **view** carries stride
`(num_spec + 1,)` — 5 at K=4. The sibling `block_table_tensor[mask, : num_spec + 1]` is
*advanced* indexing and therefore a copy, which is why the speculative path never trips.

**And the existing guard cannot work.** `mamba/ops/cpu/gdn_attention.py` already has
`state_indices_tensor = state_indices_tensor.contiguous()` for exactly this, but when the
batch holds a single non-spec decode the tensor has one element, and PyTorch reports
`is_contiguous() == True` for any tensor with `numel <= 1` regardless of stride — so it
returns `self` and the stride-5 view reaches the kernel untouched. The bug hides behind a
line that looks like the fix.

Confirmed by forcing a genuine packed copy (`torch.empty(...).copy_(...)`, **not**
`.contiguous()`) on the read-only index arguments: the contiguity error disappears. That
repack is what let me reach your code path at all. Suggested fix is to pack it at the
producer in `gdn_attn.py`, or check `stride(-1) == 1` explicitly at the call site;
`.contiguous()` is not sufficient anywhere a length-1 batch is possible.

## One correctness question on the clamp

The clamp stops the crash, and I want to be clear I verified that and not more. It also
silently changes which history window is read for a shrunken step. Across 14 requests I saw
no garbage output, but that does not establish the conv state stays numerically correct under
sustained clamping — my runs can't distinguish "correct" from "plausible". Since the
underlying inconsistency looks like it originates in `build()` — `spec_query_start_loc` is
this step's scheduled tokens while `num_accepted_tokens` is the previous step's sampler
result, with nothing tying them together — it may be worth deciding whether the conv path
should tolerate the pair or the metadata should never emit it. Not a blocker on this PR from
where I sit; it fixes a real crash and I'd take it.

Caveat on my setup, unchanged: I backport your Python file onto a released CPU image rather
than building `main`, so `_custom_ops.py` and the C++ kernel stay at that release. If `main`
also moved those, discount accordingly.

Happy to run anything else against this reproduction.

@ixcans Thanks for the A/B — 3/12 dead vs 12/12 clean on the same rig is the proof this needed, and the varying overshoot (num_accepted up to 5 against q_i of 2-3) settles why a fixed offset was never the right shape. The warning firing exactly on the over-contract cases and nowhere else is the behavior the field report wanted.

With your corner covered and CI green, this is ready for maintainer review on my side.

This pull request has merge conflicts that must be resolved before it can be
merged. Please rebase the PR, @he-yufeng.

https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/working-with-forks/syncing-a-fork

Rebuilt this on current main (`e4a5b55373`) and pushed `2697107688`. The conflict is resolved and GitHub now reports the PR as mergeable.

The rebuild also caught a semantic problem in my earlier clamp. `num_accepted` describes the previous step, while `q_i` is the current step's query length. Current main's `test_spec_forward_conv_tracks_accepted_tokens` explicitly exercises a valid row where the previous acceptance count is larger than the current query length, and that test failed with `min(acc, q_i)`. The fallback now clamps only to the actual stored history, not to current `q_i`. Zero acceptance still uses offset 0 and skips the state roll; acceptance beyond the stored history uses the latest valid window.

Local verification on this head is 11 passed for the related Python spec/conv tests, including that existing cross-step regression and the three new cases. Ruff and diff checks pass. The native parameter case cannot run in this checkout because its `_C` binary lacks `causal_conv1d_weight_pack`, so I am not claiming a whole-file or native-hardware pass.

@ixcans your earlier A/B established the crash fix on the previous head. If your rig is available, a retest of this rebuilt head would be useful because it preserves the valid shrunken-step history instead of clamping it to current `q_i`.
